blockers: Line 148-163 in app/qttunebridge.cpp: Thread safety violation - m_currentFrameCount is a non-atomic int accessed from worker thread (read) and GUI thread (write). Without proper synchronization, this creates a data race.

Line 148-163 in app/qttunebridge.cpp: Queue overflow handling removed - the old code had m_inFlightFrames with MaxInFlightFrames=1000 to bound queued frames. The new code removes this backpressure mechanism, allowing unbounded queue growth if GUI thread is slow.

Line 148-163 in app/qttunebridge.cpp: Race condition in backpressure check - onFrame reads m_currentFrameCount which is only incremented in handleFrameInternal (GUI thread). Multiple queued frames can pass the check before any are processed, exceeding MaxFrames.
questions: What is the intended backpressure strategy now that m_inFlightFrames is removed? The old mechanism bounded queued frames; the new code has no equivalent protection against event queue overflow.
Should m_currentFrameCount be atomic, or is there a different synchronization strategy planned?

The comment on line 161 states 'frame is stack-owned by mock_worker' - is this guarantee enforced by the C API contract? What prevents the frame from being invalidated before the queued lambda executes?
nits: Line 161 in app/qttunebridge.cpp: Consider adding an explicit comment explaining why the frame copy is safe, or document the contract with the mock worker.
Consider restoring the m_inFlightFrames mechanism or an equivalent queue depth counter to prevent unbounded memory growth.
The forceFrameCountForTesting method was removed - is there an alternative way to test edge cases around the MaxFrames boundary?
